title: OpenAI Chat Completions compatibility: request/response orchestrator with streaming backpressure
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary: Build an orchestrator component that translates OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) request/response shape and semantics into Redwood's internal streaming and tool-calling primitives. The orchestrator must preserve: 1) streaming token granularity and SSE framing expectations so legacy clients receive tokens and function_call deltas the way they expect; 2) function/tool invocation semantics (function_call suggestions, arguments, tool response injection) with idempotency and backpressure; 3) structured output enforcement and schema-driven post-processing; and 4) error semantics and status codes mapping. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, telemetry, and a staged rollout plan for the orchestrator component.

Rationale: Many customers run legacy clients against Redwood's API expecting OpenAI ChatCompletions wire semantics. Existing adapters normalize a subset of fields but edge cases around mid-stream function_call deltas, partial JSON output, and retry ordering cause application-visible regressions. This orchestrator aims to be a single component that centralizes mapping rules, provides clear opt-in compatibility flags, and emits detailed telemetry for regressions.

Scope:
- Request mapping: messages, system/user/assistant roles, top_level parameters (max_tokens, temperature, top_p, n, stop, presence/ frequency penalties), streaming flag, function_call hinting ("none" | "auto" | {name}), and logit_bias.
- Response mapping: SSE framing, delta token envelopes, function_call start/args/end deltas, final structured content, finish_reason mapping.
- Tool/function calling: coordinate with Redwood tool runtime to queue tool runs, stream tool stdout/stderr deltas to clients when appropriate, and support tool-level backpressure so streaming generation pauses until tool returns or a timeout triggers fallback.
- Idempotency and ordering: ensure request_id + seq counters for replays and hedging; deterministic boundary markers for partial function_call argument emissions.
- Compatibility flags: allow per-api-key opt-in to strict OA-CC semantics vs. Redwood-native semantics.
- Tests & metrics: integration suite simulating legacy clients + tooling, e2e latency benchmarks, and compatibility regression alerts.

Important constraints: preserve low tail latency for streaming (target: <5ms median added overhead for mapping) and avoid amplification of token emission rate that would increase customer costs.
acceptance_criteria: All OA-CC request parameters listed in scope are accepted and translated into internal job definitions
Streaming responses produce equivalent SSE event sequences for representative legacy clients (unit tests + integration harness)
Function_call lifecycle: suggestion -> args stream -> tool invocation -> tool result injection -> final message reconstructed; validated with synthetic tool harness
At-edge feature flag to enable/disable OA-CC strict mode per API key
Automated compatibility test matrix (10 representative prompts, 3 tool behaviours) is green in CI
Telemetry emits compatibility.mapping.* events and a dashboard exists for rollforward regressions
Performance: mapping layer adds <5ms median latency and <20ms 95th percentile for typical 256-token streams
technical_notes:
Request translation rules (high level):
- messages[] -> internal turns[]: map role names exactly, preserve metadata.name and content.types. If messages contain 'tool' role (legacy misuse), coerce to 'assistant' + tag 'legacy_tool_role'.
- max_tokens -> internal.max_new_tokens; if client sends both max_tokens and stop sequences, ensure we apply stop-based truncation post-generation.
- streaming=true: create a token-streamer wrapper that listens to the runtime token events and emits OA-CC style 'data: {"choices":[{"delta":...}]}'
- function_call: if request.function_call == "auto" or {name}, forward hint to planner; stream 'delta' fragments with 'function_call' partial args as text until closed. Use bracketed arg chunks with sequence_id to reconstruct.

Edge cases and decisions:
- Partial JSON from model during generation: buffer until bracket/brace balance heuristics indicate JSON block is likely complete, then emit 'function_call' args close. Conservative buffering default is 256 chars or 200ms - tunable via config.
- Tool backpressure: if tool takes > 1500ms, emit a 'tool-wait' intermediate delta event so client UIs can show progress; also configurable timeout per API-key.
- Retries and hedging: when hedging duplicates token streams, use request_id + origin_shard_id to deduplicate on the client-facing stream.
- Failure mapping: map internal transient errors to 5xx with an OA-CC style error envelope; map authorization to 401/403 per OA-CC.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 0 (design): finalize mapping table, event envelope shapes, and config knobs (2 days).
- Phase 1 (shim runtime): implement streaming envelope generator and request translator, unit tests for mapping rules (6 days).
- Phase 2 (function orchestration): implement function_call arg stream reassembly, tool invocation queueing with backpressure hooks (8 days).
- Phase 3 (integration & telemetry): end-to-end harness, dashboards, and canary rollout (6 days).
- Phase 4 (rollout): staged rollout: internal customers -> limited public opt-in keys -> default opt-in for new keys -> opt-out deprecation window (2 weeks total cadence).
rollout_plan:
Canary plan: 1) Merge behind feature-flag and alpha rollout to internal beta orgs; 2) Enable for 5% of production traffic on non-critical routes; 3) Monitor compatibility.metrics for 48h, rollback if error_rate > 0.5% or user-reported regressions emerge; 4) Gradually increase to 25% -> 50% -> 100% across regions with metric gates; 5) For Dedicated/Private customers, release as a minor version and coordinate with SEs for toggles. Communication: release notes, migration guide, and an opt-out API key flag.

Monitoring & Alerting:
- Dashboards: compatibility.mapping.success_rate, mapping.latency.p50/p95, function_call.tool_latency, mapping.error_classes by route
- Alerts: error_rate delta > 0.3% vs baseline, p95 latency increase > 30ms, function_call failures > 0.5%
